name: What finishes last longest in a custom spa: tile, plaster, or stone?

mainEntity.name: What finishes last longest in a custom spa: tile, plaster, or stone?
mainEntity.text: What finishes last longest in a custom spa: tile, plaster, or stone?

acceptedAnswer.text: The longest-lasting spa finish is usually the one that is installed correctly and maintained consistently. Tile can deliver a premium look and strong durability, especially when the waterproofing and setting materials are high quality. Plaster can be attractive and cost-effective, but it may need resurfacing sooner depending on water chemistry and usage. Natural stone can look exceptional in luxury projects, though it needs proper sealing, detailing, and maintenance to avoid staining or wear. For custom spa construction, the finish choice should be matched to climate, style, maintenance tolerance, and budget. The key is not just the visible surface but also what is behind it: waterproofing, substrate preparation, expansion details, and drainage. Homeowners should ask how the contractor handles finish transitions, maintenance expectations, and what the warranty covers. A beautiful finish that is hard to service can become expensive later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tile, plaster, and stone each perform differently, but durability depends more on installation quality, waterproofing, and maintenance than on the surface alone. High-quality tile systems often hold up well, while poorly installed finishes fail early.
